newsitem.title: GERMANY: Serb president says don't link aid to Karadzic.
newsitem.headline: Serb president says don't link aid to Karadzic.

text.p: Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic told German television on Thursday the international community should not make promised aid contingent on the arrest of former president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic.

"The behaviour of the donors is inhumane. The money should not be for Karadzic, rather for the people who need it for reconstruction," Plavsic told ZDF television in an interview, according to a translation of her comments into German.
Some 48 countries and 30 international institutions this week pledged $1.22 billion to aid reconstruction in Bosnia.

But the Serb Republic, the autonomous entity which splits post-war Bosnia with a Moslem-Croat federation, was denied aid until it cooperates fully with all aspects of the Dayton peace treaty that ended the 1992-95 war, including the handover of indicted war criminals.
Plavsic also defended her recent dissolution of parliament, disputed by hardliners loyal to Karadzic.

"If you say it is against the constitution to dissolve parliament, although it is written in the constitution, then you could also say that a ban on extradition is also against the constitution," she said in a veiled reference to Karadzic.
Serb authorities have not delivered any indictees and contend they only defended the Serb nation in war and say the Serb Republic constitution forbids extradition of its citizens.

Plavsic has been locked in a power struggle with Karadzic's allies ever since her outspoken attacks on the former president at rallies and her comments in an interview threatening to arrest Karadzic and his allies for rampant corruption.
Bosnian Serb ultra-nationalists loyal to Karadzic expelled Plavsic from the ruling Serb Democratic Party (SDS) on Saturday and demanded she step down from office.
She has dissolved parliament and called new elections for September 1, but Karadzic loyalists have refused to recognise her decision and say they will hold a parliamentary session next month.
